title: SVT: vagal manoeuvres and adenosine
stem: A 30-year-old woman has had sudden-onset regular palpitations for 40 minutes. HR 190, BP 112/70, RR 18, SpO2 99%. No chest pain, no breathlessness, no dizziness. Manage her.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring on; any adverse features? Read the ECG.

phases.title: Vagal manoeuvre
phases.goal: Try the modified Valsalva first, properly.

phases.title: Adenosine
phases.goal: Set up, warn her, record the strip, then adenosine from the drug cart — and escalate if it fails.

phases.title: After
phases.goal: A 12-lead in sinus rhythm: what does it show, and what does she need?

notes:
Checked against RCUK tachycardia algorithm (2021; unchanged 2025), ESC 2019 SVT guidelines and the REVERT trial (Lancet 2015).

Stable regular narrow complex tachycardia: vagal manoeuvres first — the modified Valsalva (REVERT): semi-recumbent, blow into a 10 mL syringe (≈40 mmHg) for 15 seconds, then lie flat with legs raised to 45° for 15 seconds; about 43% convert versus 17% with standard Valsalva. Carotid sinus massage only without bruits or cerebrovascular history (avoid in older patients).

Adenosine: 6 mg rapid IV bolus into a large proximal vein with a 20 mL saline flush, under continuous ECG recording; if unsuccessful 12 mg, then 18 mg (RCUK; AHA uses 6 then 12). Warn the patient about brief chest discomfort, flushing and a sense of doom. Caution in severe asthma (verapamil is an alternative). Reduce the dose (start 3 mg) with dipyridamole, carbamazepine, heart transplant or a central line.

After conversion, look for pre-excitation (short PR, delta wave): WPW needs cardiology referral for ablation, and AV-node blockers must be avoided if she ever presents with pre-excited AF.

Your SVT notes list adult DC cardioversion energies from AHA (100 J for narrow complex); that applies only if unstable.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Put her on the monitor: ECG leads, NIBP cuff and SpO2 probe.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

ABCDE.r: No shock, no syncope, no chest pain, no heart failure.
Two brief episodes before that stopped on their own. No asthma. No regular medicines.
ABCDE.mark: Asks about asthma and interacting drugs

ECG.r: Regular narrow complex tachycardia at 190, no visible P waves.

steps.label: Modified Valsalva
steps.hint: Semi-recumbent, blow into a syringe 15 s, then flat with legs up 15 s.

opts.performHint: Do it with her. The strain has to be long and the legs go up at once.
mark: Strain at about 40 mmHg for 15 s
Leg raise after the strain (modified Valsalva)

steps.label: Trolley
steps.hint: A large proximal vein and a fast flush.

opts.t: Cannula in the antecubital fossa; 3-way tap with a 20 mL saline flush

steps.label: Talk to her
steps.hint: Warn her what adenosine feels like.

opts.t: Warn her: brief chest tightness, flushing, a feeling of doom
opts.tz: 我會打一支藥令個心跳暫停一兩秒，你會覺得心口好翳、面熱、好似好驚，但係好快就會過。

steps.label: Nurse
steps.hint: Record the rhythm through the push.

opts.t: Record a rhythm strip through the push.
opts.mark: 6 mg rapid bolus with flush, recording

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Rapid push into a proximal vein, flushed straight after; escalate if it fails.

opts.t: Adenosine 6 mg rapid IV push, then flush
opts.dose: 6 mg rapid IV push, then flush
opts.r: The monitor pauses for two seconds… then SVT again at 190.
opts.mark: Adenosine 6 mg rapid push with flush

opts.t: Adenosine 12 mg rapid IV push, then flush
opts.dose: 12 mg rapid IV push, then flush

opts.r: Adenosine's half-life is seconds; it must be a rapid bolus into a large vein.
opts.t: Adenosine 6 mg slowly over a minute

opts.r: Too little here: 3 mg is for a central line, dipyridamole or a heart transplant. Start with 6 mg.

ECG.r: Short PR interval with a slurred upstroke (delta wave) and a slightly broad QRS: pre-excitation.

steps.label: Talk to Ms Ip
steps.hint: Explain, teach the manoeuvre, refer to cardiology for ablation.

opts.t: Explain WPW; cardiology referral for an electrophysiology study and ablation
opts.tz: 你心電圖見到有一條額外嘅電線路，叫 WPW，所以心跳會突然好快。我會轉介你去心臟科，做電生理檢查，可能可以用導管燒斷條額外線路。

opts.t: Teach her the modified Valsalva for future episodes; return if it fails or she feels faint
opts.tz: 我教你一個方法：用力谷氣十五秒，然後即刻瞓低、對腳舉高。下次再心跳快可以試吓；如果唔得，或者覺得就嚟暈，就要即刻返嚟。

opts.t: Start regular verapamil to prevent episodes
opts.tz: 我開 verapamil 俾你日日食，預防再發作。
opts.r: AV-node blockers can be dangerous with pre-excitation if AF develops.

qs.q: Modified Valsalva conversion rate in REVERT?

wrong: Beta-blockers or verapamil in the last day

qs.q: Why avoid AV-node blockers in pre-excited AF?
qs.a: Conduction speeds down the accessory pathway, risking VF
wrong: They trigger bronchospasm in most patients with WPW
They cause complete heart block in pre-excitation
They are ineffective but otherwise safe to try

qs.a: Short PR, delta wave, broad QRS
wrong: Long PR, narrow QRS, U waves
ST elevation in V1–V3 with RBBB
Peaked T waves and flat P waves

badge.name: Vagus Nerve
badge.flavor: Blow, then legs up. Rapid push, fast flush. Look for the delta wave.

cards.q: Modified Valsalva: after 15 s of strain the patient…
options: Lies flat with legs raised to 45° for 15 s
Sits upright and coughs hard for 15 s
Holds the breath for 60 s while sitting
Drinks iced water while lying on the left side
cards.why: REVERT: the leg raise increases venous return and vagal tone.

cards.q: First adenosine dose for adult SVT?

options: Rapidly into a large proximal vein with a flush
Slowly over 5 minutes through a small hand vein

cards.q: Delta wave is a sign of…
cards.why: Slurred upstroke from early ventricular activation via the accessory pathway.
